svg.title: Allocate a $45,000 Reference Budget Before the First Offer
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-07-forty-five-thousand-dollar-startup-stack; chart type: stacked_comparison; title: Allocate a $45,000 Reference Budget Before the First Offer; subtitle: Four capital buckets: $15,000 lean, $45,000 reference, $75,000 expanded; chapter number: 4; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Numeric values represent the $45,000 central startup plan inside the canonical $15,000–$75,000 USD capital range. Each bucket also states its lean and expanded allocations; these are alternative budgets, not additive funding sources. Values are capital allocations, not annual expenses or recognized revenue. Acquisition capital remains inventory until disposition; unused reserves remain cash. Startup parcel prices must fit available cash rather than assume the mature Base-Case purchase price. Recycling sale proceeds is required to support annual purchases above the initial inventory bucket.; caption: Lean: $6,000 + $1,500 + $1,500 + $6,000 = $15,000. Reference: $24,000 + $4,500 + $1,500 + $15,000 = $45,000. Expanded: $42,000 + $7,500 + $3,000 + $22,500 = $75,000. The reference operating reserve covers three months at $5,000 monthly, not the entire 3–9 month first-deal window under every timing outcome.; stages: label: Parcel purchase capital; value: Lean $6,000; reference $24,000; expanded $42,000; numeric value: 24000.0; detail: Allocate $6,000 in the $15,000 lean plan, $24,000 in the $45,000 reference plan, or $42,000 in the $75,000 expanded plan to purchase prices and deposits credited against those prices. The reference bucket cannot fund the mature Base-Case $30,000 average purchase outright; target lower-priced inventory without consuming reserves. Do not count pending sales as available acquisition cash.; label: Diligence and preparation; value: Lean $1,500; reference $4,500; expanded $7,500; numeric value: 4500.0; detail: Allocate $1,500 in the $15,000 lean plan, $4,500 in the $45,000 reference plan, or $7,500 in the $75,000 expanded plan to surveys, environmental work, land-use verification, and narrowly scoped preparation. Track failed-deal investigation costs separately from successful parcel basis, and stop spending when a fatal defect emerges. Reject or separately fund scopes exceeding the available diligence allocation.; label: Closing and carrying liquidity; value: Lean $1,500; reference $1,500; expanded $3,000; numeric value: 1500.0; detail: Allocate $1,500 in the $15,000 lean plan, $1,500 in the $45,000 reference plan, or $3,000 in the $75,000 expanded plan to settlement charges, property taxes, insurance, and parcel-specific carrying bills before sales replenish cash. Confirm transaction-specific costs before committing capital. Do not also allocate this same cash to recurring contractor or software invoices.; label: Operating runway; value: Lean $6,000; reference $15,000; expanded $22,500; numeric value: 15000.0; detail: Allocate $6,000 in the $15,000 lean plan, $15,000 in the $45,000 reference plan, or $22,500 in the $75,000 expanded plan to recurring operations. Lean runway is two months at $3,000 monthly; reference and expanded runway are three and 4.5 months at $5,000 monthly. The canonical monthly range is $3,000–$15,000, and time to first deal is 3–9 months; resale cash may arrive later. These reserves do not guarantee funding through exit. Close any projected cash shortfall before committing to purchases by reducing spending or securing funding.

text.title: Allocate a $45,000 Reference Budget Before the First Offer
text.tspan: Allocate a $45,000 Reference Budget Before the First

rect.title: label: Parcel purchase capital; numeric value: 24000.0; value: Lean $6,000; reference $24,000; expanded $42,000; detail: Allocate $6,000 in the $15,000 lean plan, $24,000 in the $45,000 reference plan, or $42,000 in the $75,000 expanded plan to purchase prices and deposits credited against those prices. The reference bucket cannot fund the mature Base-Case $30,000 average purchase outright; target lower-priced inventory without consuming reserves. Do not count pending sales as available acquisition cash.

text.title: Parcel purchase capital: Lean $6,000; reference $24,000; expanded $42,000
text.tspan: Parcel purchase capital: Lean $6,000; reference $24,000; expanded $42,000

rect.title: label: Diligence and preparation; numeric value: 4500.0; value: Lean $1,500; reference $4,500; expanded $7,500; detail: Allocate $1,500 in the $15,000 lean plan, $4,500 in the $45,000 reference plan, or $7,500 in the $75,000 expanded plan to surveys, environmental work, land-use verification, and narrowly scoped preparation. Track failed-deal investigation costs separately from successful parcel basis, and stop spending when a fatal defect emerges. Reject or separately fund scopes exceeding the available diligence allocation.

text.title: Diligence and preparation: Lean $1,500; reference $4,500; expanded $7,500
text.tspan: Diligence and preparation: Lean $1,500; reference $4,500; expanded $7,500

rect.title: label: Closing and carrying liquidity; numeric value: 1500.0; value: Lean $1,500; reference $1,500; expanded $3,000; detail: Allocate $1,500 in the $15,000 lean plan, $1,500 in the $45,000 reference plan, or $3,000 in the $75,000 expanded plan to settlement charges, property taxes, insurance, and parcel-specific carrying bills before sales replenish cash. Confirm transaction-specific costs before committing capital. Do not also allocate this same cash to recurring contractor or software invoices.

text.title: Closing and carrying liquidity: Lean $1,500; reference $1,500; expanded $3,000
text.tspan: Closing and carrying liquidity: Lean $1,500; reference $1,500; expanded $3,000

rect.title: label: Operating runway; numeric value: 15000.0; value: Lean $6,000; reference $15,000; expanded $22,500; detail: Allocate $6,000 in the $15,000 lean plan, $15,000 in the $45,000 reference plan, or $22,500 in the $75,000 expanded plan to recurring operations. Lean runway is two months at $3,000 monthly; reference and expanded runway are three and 4.5 months at $5,000 monthly. The canonical monthly range is $3,000–$15,000, and time to first deal is 3–9 months; resale cash may arrive later. These reserves do not guarantee funding through exit. Close any projected cash shortfall before committing to purchases by reducing spending or securing funding.

Acquisition capital remains inventory until disposition; unused reserves remain cash. Startup parcel prices must fit available cash rather than assume the mature Base-Case purchase price. Recycling sale proceeds is required to support annual purchases above the initial inventory bucket.
